_note: v2 hook overrides for le Labyrinthe de buis (B56_labyrinthe). Every hook describes what is actually painted (nothing is written in the paintings).

fr_la_adv.hook: "Over THERE!" ("LA") sings a little tour guide in a blue coat, waving his closed umbrella towards the far end of the maze: "La, la, la!"
fr_la_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted guide is a boy in a blue coat, arm up, umbrella in hand.

fr_ici_adv.hook: A pirate digs and shouts "Easy ("ee-SEE")! The treasure's right HERE!" as the chest appears in the hole at his feet.
fr_ici_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the half-dug treasure chest is painted beside his spade.

fr_moins_adv.hook: "MWAN" sounds like "MOAN": the shopkeeper in the little kiosk MOANS, head in his hands, because his cash drawer holds LESS and LESS, just one coin left. Moins = LESS, and MINUS in sums: dix moins deux font huit.
fr_moins_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted kiosk keeper holds his cheeks over an almost empty cash drawer.

fr_loin_adv.hook: A lion ("LWAN") roars FAR away on a hill on the horizon, way beyond the maze.

fr_autour_adv.hook: "Oh, a tour!" ("oh-TOOR"): a little red tour train puffs AROUND and around the round topiary ball in the maze.
fr_autour_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a little tour train circling a round topiary, not a bus and statue.

fr_surtout_adv.hook: A bear at the cake stall begs: "SIR, TWO ("sur-TOO") slices, ESPECIALLY of the big chocolate cake!"
fr_surtout_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted bear hugs a chocolate cake at a stall in the maze.

fr_la_bas_adv.hook: A sheep on a far hill bleats "La-BAA!": it's OVER THERE, out of reach beyond the maze.

fr_partout_adv.hook: A party EVERYWHERE ("pahr-TOO"): children in party hats throw confetti, and it lands on the hedges, the path, everywhere.
fr_partout_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the confetti party is painted by three children in party hats.

fr_pres_adv.hook: A praying mantis ("PREH") sits NEAR a sleeping kitten on a stone bench, so close their noses almost touch.
fr_pres_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the bench is painted in the middle of a hedge loop.

fr_au_dessus_adv.hook: "Oh, the Sue ("oh-duh-SEW")!" Sue floats ABOVE the hedge maze on a bunch of balloons.

fr_exclusivement_adv.hook: Like English 'exclusively', said ehk-sklew-zee-vuh-MAHN: one low hedge tunnel in the maze is EXCLUSIVELY for snails, and a line of them slides through it.
fr_exclusivement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a hedge tunnel with a line of snails (no sign).

fr_par_ci_adv.hook: "pahr-SEE": a rabbit hops par-ci, par-là, HERE AND THERE through the maze with a sprig of PARSLEY in its mouth, dropping more sprigs along the path.
fr_par_ci_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the dropped parsley sprigs are painted along the rabbit's path.

fr_entre_temps_adv.hook: MEANWHILE on the little hedge stage: "Enter, Tom!" ("on-truh-TON"). Tom stands ready while, in the meantime, two stagehands whizz the cardboard tree round on its wheels.
fr_entre_temps_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the backstage scene is painted as the open-air hedge stage at the heart of the maze.

fr_separement_adv.hook: Like English 'separately', said say-pah-ray-MAHN: two cats come into the maze SEPARATELY, from two different gaps, and meet nose to nose in the middle.

fr_intimement_adv.hook: Like English 'intimately', said an-tee-muh-MAHN: a squirrel on the hedge top knows the maze INTIMATELY, every turn and every acorn hidden along the hedges.
fr_intimement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the hidden acorns are painted tucked into the hedge below him.

fr_idem_adv.hook: Like English 'idem', said ee-DEHM: twin hedgehogs order exactly the same thing, a pink ice-cream each: "Ditto! IDEM!"
fr_idem_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted twins each hold an identical pink ice-cream cone.

fr_incognito_adv.hook: Like English 'incognito', said an-koh-nyee-TOH: a girl walks INCOGNITO through the maze in a round hedge costume, but her smiling face peeks out and gives her away.
fr_incognito_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: no bare toe is painted; her face and one hand peek out of the costume.

fr_socialement_adv.hook: Like English 'socially', said soh-syah-luh-MAHN: two badgers lean over a hedge and chat SOCIALLY, sharing one biscuit.
fr_socialement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows two badgers rather than hedgehogs (the hedgehogs are the idem twins).

fr_au_devant_adv.hook: "Oh, the van!" ("oh-duh-VAHN"): through the tower window a delivery van parks right IN FRONT of the tower, and the gardener's boy runs out to meet it.
fr_au_devant_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted van is seen through the tower window.

fr_au_dedans_adv.hook: "Oh! The DEN!" ("oh-duh-DAHN"): a bear cub snuggles deep INSIDE its cosy straw den, only its face peeping out.
fr_au_dedans_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted den is a round straw den inside the tower; no snow is painted.

fr_deca_adv.hook: A carpenter boy keeps his saw ("duh-SAH") ON THIS SIDE of the little picket fence, pointing to it: over here!

fr_ci_joint_adv.hook: "SEE, JOINED!" ("see-ZHWAN"): on the table a letter has a photo paper-clipped to it, ENCLOSED HEREWITH, and the pigeon postman waits to take it.
fr_ci_joint_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the pigeon postman is painted beside the letter.

fr_specifiquement_adv.hook: Like English 'specifically', said spay-see-fee-kuh-MAHN: a mole on a stool points his stick at one tiny red cross on the maze map: SPECIFICALLY there, nowhere else.
fr_specifiquement_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted map has a red cross rather than an X.
